author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A 47-year-old Afghan woman who held lawful permanent residency in the United States has been deported in the first case pursued through the Alien Terrorist Removal Court, Reuters reported Friday. The little-used court was created in 1996 to handle government efforts to remove people accused of terrorism-related activity.

The Justice Department accused Nazira Haji Zada of helping conceal a failed Islamic State-inspired plan for a mass shooting on Election Day 2024. She was not criminally charged. Her son and son-in-law pleaded guilty in related cases. Proceedings in the special court can include classified evidence that the person facing removal is not permitted to review, a structure her public defender challenged on due-process grounds.

Haji Zada agreed last month to end her challenge and consent to removal. Chief Judge Joan Ericksen approved the request, clearing the way for deportation. Her attorney said the agreement should not be read as an endorsement of the court or its procedures. The case establishes a new precedent for a tribunal that had not previously been used in the three decades since Congress created it, and it may draw further legal scrutiny.
dek: The Justice Department used a court created in 1996 for the first time to remove a lawful permanent resident accused of helping conceal a terrorism plot.
headline: U.S. deports Afghan woman in first use of terrorism removal court
